FINDING (medium, correctness): Some top-level entries are under-classified as read-only even though their command surfaces are not read-only. Evidence: [command_guidance.py](/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic-agent-command-surface/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/command_guidance.py:128) marks `agent` read-only while [command_validation.py](/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic-agent-command-surface/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/command_validation.py:274) documents `agent register-worker` as a guarded role-assignment write path; [command_guidance.py](/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic-agent-command-surface/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/command_guidance.py:142) marks `mcp` read-only while its example is `mcp serve` and [cli.py](/Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic-agent-command-surface/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/cli.py:1872) says it starts the local MCP server. Recommendation: classify top-level commands conservatively by their riskiest supported subcommand, or make the inventory path-aware for subcommands so `agent brief` and `agent register-worker` can carry distinct metadata.
